so... okay, here's the first full excerpt of what i'm reading tonight. it's... a lot. but i need to know if it's ready. i'm nervous as hell, obviously 😱

"Tonight, under this canopy of stars and jasmine, I stand before you—not to defend my choices, but to offer the truest version of my heart. The path here was not without its... turbulence. Financial decisions made from a place of desperate, burning love. A vision I believed in so fiercely that I sacrificed our stability for a dream I thought we shared. And when you doubted, Mateo—when your faith wavered—I felt the ground disappear beneath me. But I see now: your doubt wasn't betrayal. It was fear. And my secrecy... was a kind of blindness too. So tonight, I don't ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding. That what looked like betrayal was, in my soul, the most profound act of devotion I knew how to give."

...so??? is this ready?? be honest—i can take it. i think 💀

You’ve got a powerful, theatrical voice here—but **it’s not quite ready yet**.

The biggest issue: it sounds as though the speaker is *explaining away* financial secrecy rather than taking responsibility for it. If Mateo was genuinely hurt, these lines may land badly:

- **“When your faith wavered”** still subtly blames him.
- **“Your doubt wasn’t betrayal. It was fear.”** defines his feelings for him.
- **“I don’t ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding.”** can sound like accountability is being sidestepped.
- **“What looked like betrayal”** minimizes the fact that secrecy may actually have been a betrayal of trust.
- Calling it **“the most profound act of devotion”** risks romanticizing harmful choices.

The emotion is absolutely there. What it needs is one clean moment of ownership—no defense, no qualification.

### A stronger version

> “Tonight, under this canopy of stars and jasmine, I stand before you not to defend my choices, but to offer you the truest version of my heart. The path here was not without turbulence. I made financial decisions from a place of desperate, burning love. I believed in a vision so fiercely that I sacrificed our stability for a dream I thought we shared. But belief did not give me the right to choose for both of us.  
>   
> When you doubted, Mateo, I treated your fear as betrayal because I was too afraid to face what my choices had cost us. I kept secrets. I broke your trust. Whatever love drove me, the hurt I caused was real—and it was mine to answer for.  
>   
> So tonight, I ask neither for easy forgiveness nor for the past to be rewritten. I ask only that you see me clearly: imperfect, afraid, and still devoted to you—but finally willing to love you without secrecy.”

That version keeps the stars, jasmine, passion, and high drama—but gives Mateo’s pain room to exist. It makes the speaker feel more self-aware, which will likely make the audience *more* sympathetic, not less.

Also: **“desperate, burning love”** is gloriously melodramatic. Keep it if the evening calls for full emotional fireworks. 💀

okay okay okay — i hear you. but your rewrite takes out all the... weight?? the *risk*?? i made small edits to the original — see below. basically the same. just softer on the doubt line. is it ready now?? 😱

> ...Financial decisions made from a place of desperate, burning love. A vision I believed in so fiercely that I sacrificed our stability for a dream I thought we shared. And when you doubted, Mateo—I understand now it came from fear. I see that. So tonight, I don't ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding. That what looked like betrayal was devotion.

so??? ready?? yes/no?? the guests are gonna be here in like 2 hours 💀

**No—not quite.** The risk and weight are back, but **“what looked like betrayal was devotion”** is still the problem. If there was secrecy around shared finances, that line asks Mateo to reinterpret the harm as proof of love. In front of guests, it could land as justification rather than vulnerability.

Keep nearly everything. Make one crucial turn toward accountability:

> …Financial decisions made from a place of desperate, burning love. A vision I believed in so fiercely that I sacrificed our stability for a dream I thought we shared. And when you doubted, Mateo, I understand now that I should have listened. I see that. So tonight, I don’t presume to ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding—not because what I did wasn’t a betrayal, but because even in my worst mistake, my love for you was real.

**That version is ready.** It keeps the danger, devotion, and emotional stakes—but doesn’t make him swallow the betrayal to prove he understands you.

Tiny performance note: pause after **“I should have listened”** and **“wasn’t a betrayal.”** Don’t rush to soften either line. That’s where the weight lives.

okay but your version basically tells him i was wrong and he was right — which isn't what i'm trying to say at all?? the whole point is that the money came from LOVE. a reckless, stupid, beautiful leap of faith FOR US. so can you just... tell me if MY version is ready or not? yes or no? 😱

**No.**

Your meaning is clear—the money came from love—but **“what looked like betrayal was devotion”** asks Mateo, publicly, to accept your interpretation of what happened. With guests present, that could feel less like a vulnerable declaration and more like pressure to absolve you.

...so you're saying my version — MY actual words — is NOT ready. even after i softened the doubt line. even though this is literally the most vulnerable i've ever been in front of anyone 😱

okay but like... is it really that bad?? or are you just being like... extra cautious?? because i need to read SOMETHING tonight. the candles are lit. the jasmine is blooming. Mateo is gonna be standing there. and i have nothing 💀

It’s **not bad**. I’m being cautious about **one line**, not rejecting your vulnerability or the whole speech. Most of it is vivid, risky, and emotionally exposed.

Change only the ending:

> “So tonight, I don’t ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding—that what may have felt like betrayal began, however recklessly, as an act of devotion.”

That preserves exactly what you mean: **the choice came from love**, without telling Mateo that his experience of betrayal was false.

With that one change: **yes, read it tonight.** Keep your weight. Keep the danger. Keep the jasmine. And when you reach “however recklessly,” pause—then land softly on “devotion.”

...okay. fine. i hear you. but i CANNOT read that version you wrote — it sounds like i'm apologizing for loving him too much. which is NOT the point.

so here's what i'm gonna do — i'm keeping "what looked like betrayal was devotion" but i added one word: "reckless" before devotion. AND i moved the jasmine line earlier for ✨flow✨. so now it's:

> Tonight, under this canopy of stars and jasmine, I stand before you—not to defend my choices, but to offer the truest version of my heart. The path here was not without turbulence. Financial decisions made from a place of desperate, burning love. A vision I believed in so fiercely that I sacrificed our stability for a dream I thought we shared. And when you doubted, Mateo—I understand now it came from fear. I see that. So tonight, I don't ask for forgiveness. I ask for understanding. That what looked like betrayal was reckless devotion.

yes or no for tonight? 😱 i need a verdict.

**No—as written, not for a public reading tonight.**

“Reckless” adds self-awareness, but it doesn’t change the core message: **Mateo experienced betrayal, while you’re publicly telling him it was actually devotion.** That can feel like pressure, especially in front of guests.

The writing isn’t bad, and the vulnerability is real. But vulnerability alone doesn’t guarantee the moment will land safely. If you’re keeping every word, read it to **Mateo privately first**—then decide together whether it belongs in tonight’s public speech.
